__
 
• **Sedimentary rock** is formed from fragments of other rocks or the remains of plants or animals, which is **option c**.
 
• **Metamorphic rock** is transformed from its original state by high pressure and temperature without melting, which corresponds to **option a**.
 
• **Igneous rock** is derived from magma that was poured out or ejected at the Earth's surface, corresponding to **option b**.

• **Sedimentary Rocks:**

 
 
• Sedimentary rocks are typically formed through the deposition of material at the Earth's surface and within bodies of water.
 
• Common processes include weathering, erosion, deposition, and lithification, which transform loose sediment into rock.
 
• Examples include limestone, shale, and sandstone, which often contain fossils and provide critical insights into the Earth's history.
 
 
 
• **Metamorphic Rocks:**
 
 
• Metamorphic rocks are formed under the surface of the Earth through the alteration of pre-existing rocks (igneous, sedimentary, or other metamorphic rocks) by high heat, pressure, and chemically active fluids.
 
• The process, called metamorphism, changes the mineral structure and texture of the rock without melting it.
 
• Examples include gneiss, schist, and marble, which are used in various construction and artistic applications.
 
 
 
• **Igneous Rocks:**
 
 
• Igneous rocks are formed from the solidification of molten magma, which cools either beneath the surface as intrusive rocks or on the surface as extrusive rocks.
 
• These rocks are primarily classified based on their composition and grain size. Common types include granite (intrusive) and basalt (extrusive).
 
• They are often valued for their hardness, durability, and in the case of pumice, for being so lightweight.

questions.question: When do the drugs used as medicines become potential poisons?

options.text: When doses are taken as recommended
When doses are taken at the recommended time and in the recommended quantity
When doses are taken higher than recommended
When doses are taken lower than recommended

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Medicines become potential poisons** when dosages exceed the levels deemed safe and effective by medical guidelines.
 
• Overdosing can lead to **toxic effects** which may cause severe organ damage or even be **fatal**.
 
• It is crucial to follow the prescribed amount and frequency to avoid adverse effects and ensure the drug's efficacy and safety.

• **Therapeutic Window: **

 
 
• Drugs have a **therapeutic window** which is the range between the minimum effective dose and the toxic dose.
 
• Staying within this window is crucial for the safe use of any medication.
 
 
 
• **Monitoring and Adjustments: **
 
 
• Regular monitoring of drug levels may be necessary, especially for medications with a narrow therapeutic window.
 
• Dose adjustments based on individual responses and interactions with other medications are vital for maintaining safety.
 
 
 
• **Risk Awareness:**
 
 
• Patients and caregivers should be educated about the risks of overdose and the importance of adhering to prescribed dosages.

questions.question: What was the symbol Henry Moseley used for denoting atomic number?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Z__**.

__
 
• Henry Moseley discovered that the atomic number of an element is a more fundamental property than its atomic mass.
 
• Moseley used the symbol Z to denote the atomic number, which represents the number of protons in an atom's nucleus.
 
• This discovery led to the reorganization of the periodic table based on atomic numbers rather than atomic masses.
 
• Moseley's work provided the foundation for the modern periodic law, which states that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Henry Moseley was an English physicist who made significant contributions to the understanding of atomic structure.
 
• His experiments with X-ray spectra allowed him to determine the charge on the nucleus of atoms, leading to the accurate determination of atomic numbers.
 
• Moseley's law mathematically related the frequency of X-rays emitted by an element to its atomic number.
 
• Tragically, Moseley was killed in World War I, cutting short a brilliant scientific career that had already had a profound impact on chemistry and physics.

questions.question: The Provincial elections were held for the first time in _______ under the Government of India Act, 1935.

__
 
• The **Provincial elections** were held for the first time in **1937** under the Government of India Act, 1935.
 
• This Act introduced provincial autonomy and abolished the system of dyarchy (dual government) in the provinces.
 
• It marked a significant step towards responsible government in India by expanding the electorate and increasing the powers of legislative councils.
 
• The 1937 elections were significant as they were the first to be held under the new system of government, and they resulted in the formation of ministries by the Indian National Congress in several provinces.

 Feature
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Government of India Act, 1935**
 Was the longest Act of British Parliament ever enacted at that time. It provided a new constitution for India.
 
 

 **Federal Structure**
 The Act proposed a federation of India, combining British India and the princely states. However, this was never implemented.
 
 

 **Reserved and Transferred Subjects**
 Introduced a division of subjects between the Central and Provincial governments into reserved and transferred subjects.
 
 

 **Bicameral Legislatures**
 Established bicameral legislatures in six provinces and introduced direct elections, thereby increasing the participation of Indians in governance.
 
 

 **Advisory Role of British Crown**
 The Viceroy retained control over matters related to defense, external affairs, and communications but acted on the advice of ministers responsible to the legislature on other matters.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Human life will be prolonged by a new drug called new-med.

options.text: A new drug called new-med was prolonging human life.
A new drug called new-med will prolong human life.
A new drug called new-med is prolonging human life.
A new drug called new-med had prolonged human life.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The type of the sentence is **declarative** and the tense of the given sentence is **future simple**.
 
• The **subject **of the given **passive **sentence is **"human life"** and the **object **is **"a new drug called new-med".**
 
• The format of passive voice for future simple tense is: **Subject + will be + V3 (past participle form of the verb) + by + Object.**
 
• The format of active voice for future simple tense is: **Subject (Objective case)+ will + V1 (base form of the verb) + object (Subjective case).**
 
• **Example: **
 
 
• "A new planet will be discovered by the scientists." (Passive Voice)
 
• "The scientist will discover a new planet." (Active Voice)
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer is- “A new drug called new-med will prolong human life.”**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
